reports.title: Salivary immunity and lower respiratory tract infections in non-elite marathon runners
reports.authors: Cantó E; Roca E; Perea L; Rodrigo-Troyano A; Suarez-Cuartin G; Giner J; Feliu A; Soria JM; Nescolarde L; Vidal S; Sibila O
source_locator: Full text PMC6248899; PLOS ONE 13(11): e0206059, published 2018-11-21
reports.inclusion_reason: Single identifiable marathon bout (2016 Barcelona Marathon, 42.195 km), pre-race baseline saliva/blood and post-race (2 days) saliva/blood samples, adults (median age 30y), direct immune-linked measures (sIgA, AMPs, chemokines, leukocyte differential).
reports.reviewer_notes: Charting-only pilot; no formal screening workbook consulted by AI stand-in C. Author's 0-72h window position of the single post sample is 48h (within window) but exact hour not reported.
reports.author_stated_use: Charting salivary IgA/AMP/chemokine profile as a potential indicator of differential immunological status associated with LRTI risk after a marathon; framed as mechanistic/exploratory, not a validated predictive tool ('Further studies are needed to better understand the underlying mechanisms...').
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.2 Introduction: 'risk of infection increased 100% to 500%...around 25% of finishers reported respiratory symptoms'
p.7 Discussion: 'may be explained by the mobilization of neutrophils to maintain blood homeostasis'

cohorts.baseline_health: Healthy non-elite marathon runners; excluded if respiratory symptoms reported in the 2 weeks before the race
cohorts.age_sex: 28 males, 19 females; mean age 39.0±7.1 y (Table 1; text also reports median age 30y)
cohorts.training_status: non-elite, experienced recreational runners; median years training ~10, ~6.5 h/week
cohorts.cohort_notes: Recruited via marathon newsletter announcement; voluntary participation.
cohorts.age_range: Mean age 39.0±7.1 y (Table 1); text states 'median age 30 years old' (internal inconsistency in the article itself)

source_locator: p.3 Methods Saliva analysis: limits of detection listed for each ELISA; 'All determinations were performed in triplicate'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Cohort-level row (applies across all saliva/blood analytes). LODs stated for every ELISA kit; triplicate analysis; explicit QC exclusion rule for IgA ratio>1. No intra-/inter-assay CV, ICC or batch-effect data reported.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Single pre-race baseline and single post-race sample (~48h after cessation)
source_locator: p.3 Methods Saliva and blood collection: 'collected one day before the marathon and two days after the end of the race'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Two time bins used: pre_exercise_baseline and 24h_to_72h_inclusive (within organising window). No immediate-post, no >72h outside-window recovery sample, no intermediate timepoints; exact hour of 'two days after' not given (day-level precision only).

source_locator: p.3 Methods: Salivary IgA, lactoferrin, lysozyme, Groα, Groβ, MCP-1 measured by ELISA; blood leukocyte differential by haematology analyzer
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Panel includes direct mucosal antibody (sIgA), antimicrobial proteins, chemokines, and blood leukocyte differential counts; all are recognised immune mediators or direct immune cell counts.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Single pre-post difference per analyte; no repeated baseline or repeat-challenge design
precision_validation.individualization: Observed individual-level changes (pre vs post) but no quantification of natural biological/analytical variation, no ICC/CV, no responder definition or repeated-baseline design
source_locator: p.3 Methods: single baseline, single post-race timepoint; no repeat-bout design
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Study design is a single bout with one pre and one post sample per person; per manual guidance this does not establish individualised/reproducible-marker status, only an observed intra-individual change.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo immune function assay performed (only concentrations and correlations)
precision_validation.temporal_order: LRTI onset occurred up to 2 weeks after saliva/blood sampling; markers measured before symptom onset; follow-up = 2 weeks
source_locator: p.2 Methods Subjects: LRTI defined per ERS/ESCMID clinical case definition, self-reported symptoms with fever and >3 days duration; no microbiological confirmation (p.8 limitations)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Lysozyme (post-race) and Groα/Groβ (non-LRTI pre-post change) differ by later LRTI status (M-R59-07, M-R59-11, M-R59-14); salivary IgA and lactoferrin showed no association with LRTI (M-R59-02, M-R59-04). Clinical endpoint is self-reported, validated case definition, no pathogen confirmation ('infectious agents that caused LRTI are not described due to the absence of microbiological studies').

precision_validation.replication: No replication cohort; single-centre, single-race, single-season study
precision_validation.prediction_design: None; descriptive/associative analysis only, no predictive model built
source_locator: p.8 Discussion limitations: 'due to the small number of runners included, the results should be validated in other studies before generalizing them'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Authors explicitly flag need for external validation; none performed in this report.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: Non-invasive saliva collection (passive pooling into sterile tub) feasible in a race-day field setting for 47 participants; blood draw required venepuncture; no cost or turnaround-time data reported
source_locator: p.3 Methods: 'Saliva was collected into clean, sterile tub...'; 'Three 10 mL blood samples were obtained from the antecubital vein'
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Field feasibility demonstrated at small scale; no explicit cost, turnaround time or real-world implementation test reported.

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable marathon bout with a pre-race baseline and a post-race sample at ~48h (within the 0-72h organising window), in healthy adults, with directly immune-linked outcomes (salivary IgA/AMPs/chemokines, blood leukocyte differential); p.2 Methods 'completed the 42.195 km...Barcelona Marathon' and p.3 'collected one day before the marathon and two days after the end of the race'. No repeated identified bouts are tracked, so Support B does not apply.

unresolved_questions: marker_family vocabulary has no category for salivary antimicrobial proteins (lactoferrin, lysozyme) distinct from cytokines/mucosal sIgA; coded as 'other' pending dictionary clarification.

precision_validation row-unit: strict per-measurement x per-domain rows would yield 22 measurements x 7 domains = 154 rows for this short paper; used cohort-level domain rows referencing representative measurements instead. Needs explicit manual guidance on intended granularity.

'Two days after the end of the race' lacks an exact hour, so placement in bin 24h_to_72h_inclusive vs a narrower/earlier bin is an approximation (day-level precision only); flagged, not UNCLEAR-coded, since 2 days unambiguously falls in that bin regardless of exact hour.

Exact number of saliva IgA determinations excluded for the ratio>1 contamination rule is not stated, so the true analytic n for IgA alone is uncertain (kept at 47 with a missing_data note rather than guessing a smaller n).

Table 1 blood/CRP values are baseline-only (LRTI vs non-LRTI at baseline), not a pre/post exercise response; included as measurements for completeness of the immune-linked candidate universe, but their relevance to 'open-window' charting (which centres on post-exercise change) is marginal and worth team discussion.
Article contains an internal inconsistency between the reported median age (30y, Results text) and Table 1 mean age (39.0±7.1y); both recorded with locators rather than reconciled by the extractor.
